findings.title: The latex-typesetter hat lost the only lawful copy of its own authoritative rulebook
findings.after: needs = ["source"]              # the persona reads the rendered policy file, never a `rulebook_sections` grant
findings.why_it_matters: The hat's persona — unchanged by this diff, so it is the promise at base — still reads: "FIRST read the house rulebook named in your substrate (the rendered policy file `latex-idiom.md`, with the package's notation parameters substituted into it) and treat it as AUTHORITATIVE". Nothing in the substrate names it any more. `rulebook` is exactly the tag that delivers the rendered policy files: `Preflight.rulebook_text` writes `rulebook.md` as `for f in Sync.POLICY_FILES … println(io, "--- rendered policy file $f ---", read(p, String))` — latex-idiom.md included — and panel.js gates both the permitted-file list (`if ((h.needs || []).includes('rulebook') && A.rulebook_path) p.push(A.rulebook_path)`) and the substrate text on it. The hat also cannot go and find the file: panel.js:69 says "Read ONLY what your substrate below grants. Unless it EXPLICITLY grants more, do NOT open src/, tests, the rulebook, memory, or anything else", and .gbg/ is closed to it besides. Every /check-consistency round from this version on runs its LaTeX-idiom hat on generic taste — the one thing its persona says it is NOT — and the RULE.TEX.* family loses its reading enforcement while the catalogue still advertises it.
findings.description: The stated reason for the edit is factually wrong about this codebase. The comment says the persona "reads the rendered policy file, never a `rulebook_sections` grant", but the `rulebook` need is not a rulebook_sections grant — it is the grant that hands over rulebook.md, whose first section IS the rendered policy files, before any rulebook_sections are appended. The real motivation is visible in resolve_hats: `("rulebook" in needs && isempty(cfg["package"]["rulebook_sections"]))` marks the hat not_applicable in a package with no rulebook sections. The defect is in that not_applicable predicate (it conflates two sources), and the fix taken instead strips the hat's rubric in every package, including the four that do declare rulebook_sections. Note the contrast with catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml, untouched at `needs = ["rulebook", "source"]`, whose persona asks for `docs-rubric.md` by exactly the same mechanism.
findings.evidence: diff: `-needs = ["source", "rulebook"]` / `+needs = ["source"]              # the persona reads the rendered policy file, never a `rulebook_sections` grant`. Persona (unchanged): "FIRST read the house rulebook named in your substrate (the rendered policy file `latex-idiom.md`, …) and treat it as AUTHORITATIVE". src/CLI/Preflight.jl: `for f in Sync.POLICY_FILES` … `println(io, "--- rendered policy file $f ---\n", read(p, String), "\n")`. panel.js:87: `if (needs.includes('rulebook')) parts.push(`THE RULEBOOK (AUTHORITATIVE — read it first, in full): ${A.rulebook_path}`)`.

findings.title: A scan that measured nothing is no longer DEAD when it has hits, contradicting its own field docstring
locations: src/Scan.jl:36-37 (the ScanResult docstring, unchanged in this respect)
findings.after:
# a scan that HIT measured something: its hits are never dropped by the dead branch
        if r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0 && isempty(r.hits)
findings.why_it_matters: A scan reporting `population == 0` alongside hits is self-contradictory: its population counter is broken. Before the diff that combination raised DEAD and exit 2 — cannot evaluate — which is precisely what surfaces a miscounted population. After it, the run reports the hits and exits 1, and the broken counter is never mentioned. The class of defect the DEAD branch exists to catch is now the class it silently swallows, in `gbg scan docs`, `gbg scan html` and `gbg round prepare` alike — and downstream in EXEMPT.BROAD, which ARCHITECTURE:1713 says "runs the predicate dry over that reported population", so an engine reporting zero "would leave it nothing to dry-run".
findings.description: The edit is wider than the defect it was written for. The defect was SCAN.FIELD_DOCS counting only structs that carried a field list, so a NOLIST hit could arrive with population 0 — and that defect is fixed independently in the same commit, by moving `checked += 1` above the `documented === nothing` branch in src/Scans/field_docs.jl. With that fix in place the report guard changes nothing for field_docs and everything for the other 41 scans: it removes the zero-population alarm from all of them. The ScanResult docstring in the same file was edited in this commit (the `note` bullet gained a lane gloss) but the `population` bullet was left promising the old behaviour, so the shipped contract and the shipped code now disagree inside one docstring. policy/testing-protocol.md RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING, unchanged, still reads "a zero count is a dead lane rather than a clean one".
findings.evidence: src/Scan.jl:36-37 at HEAD, untouched: "- `population` — what the scan measured (files, docstrings, exports, arguments or pages); zero means the scan measured nothing and is DEAD." src/Scans/field_docs.jl in the same diff: `+            checked += 1                                          # every struct opened was checked: a` / `-            checked += 1` (moved out of the post-NOLIST path).

findings.title: CFG.SURFACES quietly stopped promising that `docs_build` names docs/make.jl
findings.before: each `extensions` file, the `docs/make.jl` that `docs_build` names, each `executable_claims` file … / `| CFG.SURFACES | … docs_build names docs/make.jl and that file exists; julia_test contains Pkg.test() …` / `docs_build  = "julia --project=docs docs/make.jl"            # CFG.SURFACES requires it to name docs/make.jl`
findings.after: each `extensions` file, the fixed path `docs/make.jl` a consumer's `docs_build` command is expected to run, each `executable_claims` file … / `| CFG.SURFACES | … the fixed path docs/make.jl a consumer's docs_build is expected to run exists; julia_test contains Pkg.test() …` / `docs_build  = "julia --project=docs docs/make.jl"            # CFG.SURFACES requires docs/make.jl to exist`
findings.why_it_matters: `check_paths` is byte-identical between base and head — the code was never changed. The only check it has ever made is `isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")`; it never inspects the `docs_build` string. So the guarantee "docs_build names docs/make.jl" was false at base and, instead of being implemented (one `occursin` beside the `Pkg.test()` check three lines away in the same function), it was deleted from three documents at once. A consumer can now set `docs_build = "julia --project=docs other/build.jl"`, keep an unused `docs/make.jl` on disk, and pass CFG.SURFACES — while `gbg round build` runs a command the tool has never verified builds the site the scans then read.
findings.description: A guarantee lost the condition it depended on. The asymmetry is the tell: the twin claim on the same line, "`julia_test` contains `Pkg.test()`", is backed by real code and survives untouched; only the claim with no code behind it was reworded away. The replacement phrasing ("the fixed path docs/make.jl a consumer's docs_build command is expected to run") is careful to state an expectation where the base stated a check, which is the shape of a promise being retired rather than kept. Nothing in the change set records the decision, and ARCHITECTURE's own text about the mandatory makedocs wrapper still assumes the two are the same file.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Config.jl at HEAD, unchanged from base: `isfile(joinpath(root, "docs", "make.jl")) || push!(errs, "package.docs_build: docs/make.jl does not exist")`; `git diff … -- src/CLI/Config.jl` shows only docstring hunks.

findings.title: SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE's "caps bind ALWAYS" weakened to match unchanged code, leaving the rule register saying "always"
findings.before:
# item `NN. ` or a `**(x) ` finding opens a new unit, so an append-only log grows by NEW units. Caps bind
# ALWAYS (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions; IT's lesson: a cap that applies only to new
# units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming).
findings.after:
# Caps
# (longest paragraph ≤ 120 words, ≤ 3 admonitions) bind on every docstring and every NEW page unit; a
# page unit already in the baseline is held by the ratchet alone, the one place IT's lesson — a cap that
# applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming — is traded for an append-only log.
findings.why_it_matters: `git diff` over src/Scans/prose_shape.jl shows one hunk, all of it comment: the `register_scan!` body is identical at base and head, and it has always read `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing` — caps on docstrings and on unbaselined page units only. The claim was wrong before and the code was not changed to meet it; the claim was rewritten to meet the code, and the escape hatch the base comment named as the reason for the strict rule ("a cap that applies only to new units is escaped by re-baselining or renaming") is now described as an accepted trade. Nothing else changed, so a rationale page whose section is in docs/prose_shape.csv can still hold a 300-word paragraph indefinitely, and after any `--rebaseline` so can a new one.
findings.description: The rewrite left the register contradicting the engine. policy/RULES.toml:231 still states RULE.DOC.SHAPE as "A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always; …", and ARCHITECTURE §12.A line 2225 repeats "admonitions ≤ 3 always", while §12.B line 2320 and the scan header now say the caps hold only for docstrings and NEW page units. One of the two must be edited; this change edited the enforcement-side description and left the rule-side statement, so the rulebook a consumer pins and the scan that is declared its check (`check = ["scan:SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE"]`, added in this same commit) now promise different things. If the weakening is the intended policy, RULE.DOC.SHAPE's statement is the place it has to be recorded; if it is not, the scan is the thing to fix.
findings.evidence: policy/RULES.toml:231 at HEAD: `statement = "A docstring's longest paragraph is at most 120 words and it has at most 3 admonitions, always; …"`. src/Scans/prose_shape.jl at HEAD, unchanged: `if occursin(" :: ", k) || b === nothing`.

findings.title: RULE.DOC.HOME_ORDER reordered fleet-wide, with both judging personas rewritten to the new order in the same commit
findings.before: A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, caveats, one formula, citation, links. … (4) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing; (5) one formula …; (6) an inline citation …; (7) cross-links.
findings.after: A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, one formula, citation, links, caveats. … (4) one formula …; (5) an inline citation …; (6) cross-links; (7) the caveats a user needs, as an admonition where load-bearing — the last substantive block, before the fields list.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the one rulebook four consumer packages pin, and the ordering it fixes is the one every function docstring in the fleet was written to. Every docstring that places its caveat admonition before the formula — the shape the rule mandated until this commit — becomes an ordering violation at the next /check-docs or /check-consistency round, without a line of prose in any of those packages changing. The rule's own enforcement class was set to `check = ["weakness"]` in the same commit, so no program will ever adjudicate which order is in force; the only thing that will is the two personas, and both were rewritten here to the new order.
findings.description: The change set contains no recorded rationale for the reorder, and it moves in the direction that makes an existing corpus compliant rather than the direction that makes it conform. The structure-consistency hat is the sharper case: its binding DIRECTION RULE, untouched, says it "is FORBIDDEN to name the majority side the norm or the minority side the defect" because "a widespread arrangement can be the wrong one, and a vote would certify it" — and this commit edits the very template it is seeded with ("e.g. one-sentence identity -> … -> caveats … -> one formula -> citation -> cross-links" becomes "… -> one formula -> citation -> cross-links -> caveats … last"), priming the hat toward one side of exactly the split it is forbidden to arbitrate. If the reorder is an owner decision it should be recorded as one; as it stands, the rule, its sentinel, its §12.A row and both judges moved together in a commit whose other work is a mass rewrite of this package's own docstrings.
findings.evidence: policy/RULES.toml diff: `-sentinel = "A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, caveats, one formula, citation, links."` / `+sentinel = "A function docstring is ordered: identity, when-to-use, arguments, one formula, citation, links, caveats."` plus `+check = ["weakness"]`. catalog/hats/structure-consistency.toml diff: `-… -> each argument -> caveats (as admonitions where load-bearing) -> one formula -> citation -> cross-links)` / `+… -> each argument -> one formula -> citation -> cross-links -> caveats (as admonitions where load-bearing), last)`.

findings.title: SCAN.SIBLING_LINK gained a second hard-tier hit class that no catalogue row, architecture row or fixture records
findings.before:
ok = m !== nothing && m.offset <= first(o) <= m.offset + ncodeunits(m.match)
            ok || push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "first mention of `$name` is not a link to $site: " * strip(raw)))
            break
findings.after:
if !seen
                seen = true
                linked || push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "first mention of `$name` is not a link to $site: " * strip(raw)))
            elseif linked
                push!(hits, Hit(file, n, "later mention of `$name` is a link, not a bare code span: " * strip(raw)))
            end
findings.why_it_matters: The scan is `tier = "hard"`, so its hits are a MUST BE EMPTY block, exit 1, and the makedocs wrapper runs the hard scans over the source surfaces before Documenter. A consumer whose page links a sibling package twice — legal under the scan until this version, and common in a page that mentions a sibling in two distant sections — now fails its docs build the moment it bumps, with no CHANGELOG line and nothing in the catalogue to say the scan's reach grew. The scan is also newly non-terminating per unit (the `break` is gone), so a unit naming a sibling ten times now yields up to nine hits where it yielded at most one.
findings.description: The underlying widening is warranted — RULE.DOC.SIBLING_LINK has always said "later mentions are bare", and the base scan enforced only half its own rule — but the change stopped at the code. ARCHITECTURE §12.B line 2314 still describes the scan as "per page, rationale document, Literate file or docstring, the first mention of each sibling must sit inside `[`Name`](site)`", with no second clause, and catalog/scans.toml still lists `fixture = ["bare-sibling"]` alone. RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS asks that a check be falsifiable by a fixture carrying a known positive; the new arm has none, so nothing in the suite would notice if `elseif linked` stopped firing. A rate-comparability note is owed too: this scan's hit counts before and after are not comparable.
findings.evidence: catalog/scans.toml:121-126 at HEAD: `id = "SCAN.SIBLING_LINK"` … `tier = "hard"` … `fixture = ["bare-sibling"]`, unchanged by this diff (`git diff … -- catalog/` touches only the three hat files).

findings.title: A ledger reason of 24-39 characters now makes the whole toolchain throw instead of the doctor reporting it
findings.why_it_matters: `Ledger.read` throws a LedgerError when the file does not validate — "an unreadable ledger is never treated as empty" — and `Scan.scan_docs` and `Scan.scan_html` call it uncaught, as does Sync through its default keyword. A consumer ledger with a 30-character reason loaded fine before this change: the entry's exemptions applied and the doctor reported `CFG.EXEMPTIONS … reason shorter than 40 characters`, naming the entry. After it, that same file makes `gbg sync`, `gbg scan` and the in-process gate throw before any diagnosis, and inside the doctor `context` swallows the error into an empty ledger, so every OTHER exemption in the file silently stops applying and unrelated exemptable FAILs stop being downgraded to WARN.
findings.description: The schema's base description recorded the division of labour deliberately — the schema held the loose floor so the doctor could report the strict bound with the offending entry named — and the edit deleted that division rather than the inconsistency it was there to manage. The tightening is defensible as an alignment with ARCHITECTURE §7.3 ("reason ≥ 40"), but it is wider than an alignment: it converts a reported, per-entry FAIL into a whole-file hard refusal across four commands, with no CHANGELOG entry and no migration note for consumer ledgers written under the 24-character floor.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Ledger.jl: `errs = validate(load_schema("exemptions"), doc); isempty(errs) || throw(LedgerError("$path is invalid:\n  " * join(errs, "\n  ")))`; src/CLI/Doctor.jl:308: `length(e["reason"]) >= 40 || push!(errs, "$tag: reason shorter than 40 characters")`; src/Scan.jl:423: `ledger = Ledger.read(cfg)` with no try.

findings.title: resolve_function's search-order promise was rewritten to match a resolution order that shadows package functions
findings.before:
and `externals`, the external modules whose generics the
package extends (searched last).
findings.after:
- `externals` — the external modules whose generics the package extends (searched after `pkg` and
  before `modules`).
findings.why_it_matters: The base docstring promised that an external module is consulted only after the package's own modules, so a package function always wins its own name. The body has never done that: `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` puts Base ahead of every package module. For this package that ordering is live — `Config.read`, `Git.run`, `Doctor.select`, `Scan.report`, `Rounds.list` all share a name with a Base export — so `resolve_function` can hand `method_parity` and `oracle_registry` the Base generic and let them count and classify the wrong function while reporting success.
findings.description: This is documentation bent to fit the code. The mismatch itself predates the diff and belongs to /bug-hunt, but the choice made inside this window does not: given a promise and a body that disagree, the edit rewrote the promise. Nothing records why externals-before-package-modules is the wanted order, and the rewritten sentence states the mechanism without stating what it costs, so the next reader has no way to tell that the ordering is a decision rather than an accident. If the order is deliberate the docstring should say why a Base generic outranks a package module; if it is not, the one-token fix is in the body.
findings.evidence: src/TestHarness.jl:303-306 at HEAD, identical to base (`git show 209cb212e9:src/TestHarness.jl | grep -n "Iterators.flatten"` → line 288): `for mod in Iterators.flatten(((pkg,), externals, modules))` / `isdefined(mod, name) || continue` / `c = getfield(mod, name)` / `c isa Function && return c`.
